reviewerStanding: INDEPENDENT of the subject's authorship: I did not author v1, v2 or v3. I DID author the predecessor verdict this successor answers (doctor-contract.v2.review-independent.json, e05493dd...). That is disclosed rather than treated as disqualifying, and it carries a specific risk this review guarded against: a reviewer checking their own findings is prone to confirmation. Every one of the four repairs below was therefore re-measured from primary sources at v3's bytes rather than compared against my own verdict's text, and I actively hunted for defects my prior verdict did not name. The one blocker raised here is NOT a survival of a v2 finding - all four v2 blockers are genuinely gone - it is a defect of the v3 generation that my prior verdict could not have named.

verdictBasis.statement: REJECT at ONE blocker. All four v2 blockers are repaired, verified by independent re-measurement rather than from the repair text. Every one of the prompt's five verification items PASSES. The single blocker is new and is about the v3 generation's accounting for itself: v3 names the verdict it answers in its own header, at digest, and then discharges that verdict invisibly - repairing five of its nine findings with no disposition recorded for any of them, and silently dropping the other four.
verdictBasis.whatThisVerdictIsNOT: It is NOT a finding that any v2 blocker survives - none does. It is NOT a finding against the design, the actor analysis, the consent model, the report schema, the outcome structure, the redaction guarantee, or the degraded-input specification, none of which v3 altered. It is NOT a recited-count or quotation-fidelity finding: v3 is clean on both, measured exhaustively. It is NOT a finding that v3 decided the actor question - it did not, and its neutrality is stronger in v3 than in v2.
verdictBasis.theRepairsAreReal: v3's repair work is precise and correct. The v2->v3 diff is 16 pointers: 4 added, 0 removed, 12 changed. Every changed pointer is a repair target or its provenance. Nothing was touched that did not need touching, and no repair overshot into the design. On craft, this is the best of the three generations.
verdictBasis.whyOneOmissionRejects: This corpus rejected v1 for a miscount that changed no conclusion, and v2 for four claims whose conclusions all survived. The standard it applies is that the RECORD is a first-class obligation, not a courtesy. A successor generation discharges its predecessor verdict through a logged disposition per finding - the institution v2 itself executed for 64 findings across two verdicts, and which v3 preserves verbatim in its own bytes while declining to apply it to its own generation. The consequence is concrete rather than formal: four findings from a named verdict received no disposition and cannot be distinguished from oversight, a fifth was repaired with no record, and a coordinator cannot audit the generation without re-deriving the diff by hand - which is precisely the labor the institution exists to remove. I did re-derive it, and that is how the omission was found.
verdictBasis.acceptGate: The blocker is ADDITIVE to fix. It requires no design change, no new measurement campaign, no re-opening of any repaired text, and not the actor decision. Adding a v2-verdict section to the repairLog with a disposition for each of B1-B4 and A1-A5, and listing the v2 verdict at /appliesFindingsOf, discharges it. A v4 doing that is reviewable on this same finding-set, and on everything else measured here it would pass.
verdictBasis.scoringNote: Scored by FINDING-SET against v3's bytes. No checker was run.

blockers.whyBlockerNotAdvisory: Four reasons. (1) A coordinator reading v3 alone, seeing a header that names the rejecting verdict at digest, will reasonably conclude the verdict was discharged - and four findings were not. A3 and A5 are one-line corrections that cost nothing; that they were skipped in a build which executed four harder repairs with precision suggests they were not seen rather than declined - and the record cannot tell a reader which. (3) The institution is not optional in this corpus and v3 knows it: it retains the full disposition vocabulary and the NOTHING IS WAIVED sentence in its own bytes, and its predecessor executed the institution for 64 findings including 12 recorded BLOCKED rather than closed by guess. Preserving the rule while exempting one's own generation from it is the defect. (4) v1 and v2 were both rejected exclusively on record defects whose conclusions survived; an unlogged generation is a larger record defect than a miscounted closed set.

I did not review the DR-105 candidate on its own merits. I read it solely to verify the join facts and enforcement census v3 asserts about it. Its own independent review recorded REJECT and is not applied here.
I did not audit the coherence review for correctness. Its findings were treated as measured input; I verified only that v3's recitals of it replicate.

I did not re-verify the substantive adequacy of all 64 v1-verdict and join-verdict repair entries. I confirmed id coverage is exact and duplicate-free and that the counts replicate; an entry could carry a disposition I would dispute on the merits without my having caught it.

I did not verify whether the four unaddressed predecessor advisories were considered and declined or simply missed. That is precisely what the missing record would have told me, and I record the ambiguity rather than resolving it by inference.

I did not execute prototype code, run any checker, or build anything. Prototype verification was limited to git HEAD, the 14 recorded digests, the CLI_DIAGNOSTIC_CODES recount, and confirmation of the recorded AGENTS.md absence.
I did not reconstruct the digest sequences the environment block records for its window; those states are not recoverable from the working tree. I verified current bytes only.

The quotation-fidelity scan covers single-quote-delimited fragments against nine corpora. It does not detect paraphrase presented as quotation, misattribution of a correctly-transcribed quote, or divergence against sources outside those nine.

I did not evaluate whether the design is right for slice 1, whether the twelve fixture classes suffice as acceptance evidence, or whether DR-114 should close. This verdict is about whether the candidate's claims replicate and whether the generation accounts for itself.

reviewSummary: REJECT at one blocker. All four v2 blockers are genuinely repaired, and I verified each from primary sources rather than from the repair text: the '17-member' claim is now a confinement statement that is true of both v2's and v3's bytes; the completeness universal is now scoped with an enumerated exclusion list that names the very reviewer-guidance growth whose concealment was the finding; the enforcement miscount is replaced by four separate sub-claims that all replicate; and every miscapitalized quotation is restored to its source characters - including a fourth occurrence inside the repairLog that my own verdict had not separately listed, which shows the repair was re-derived rather than transcribed. Advisory A1 was repaired too. On the prompt's five items v3 passes all five: no new recited count fails - I recomputed every one - and all 252 precisely-delimited quotations resolve exactly, with zero case divergences; the actor question is still not decided and the neutrality language is stronger than v2's; the DR-105 tokens remain wholly confined at 28 occurrences with none outside; and no D9 or exit value is minted. The repair work itself is the best of the three generations - 16 pointers touched, every one a repair target or its provenance, nothing overshooting into the design. What fails is that this generation does not account for itself. v3 adds exactly four top-level members, all of them provenance naming the rejecting verdict at digest, and then discharges that verdict invisibly: no repair-log section, no entry at appliesFindingsOf, no disposition for any of its nine findings. Five were repaired with no record and four were dropped with no word - which in this corpus's own vocabulary is waiving, under a sentence the artifact still carries saying nothing is waived. I recovered the dispositions by diffing v2 against v3, which is exactly the labor the repair-log institution exists to remove and which v2 performed for sixty-four findings. The fix is additive and touches no repaired text: a predecessor-verdict section in the repairLog and the verdict listed at appliesFindingsOf. On everything else measured here, a v4 doing that would pass.
